O'Shaquie Foster delivered one of the year's most impressive boxing performances on Saturday, taming the unrelenting ferocity of Emanuel Navarrete to win a lopsided decision and become the WBC, WBO and IBF unified super featherweight champion at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio.
 It was a satisfying fight in more ways than one — an 130-pound epic featuring two of the most talented fighters in the sport, and a performance of the year contender for Foster. But it was also a much-needed display from Top Rank, the longtime promotional entity which spent the bulk of last year broadcast-homeless. On Saturday, however, Top Rank gave its new platform, DAZN, a taste of what it can perhaps expect, through its conveyor belt of up-and-coming talents, and, of course, its present-day champions.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In 2026, boxing appears to have produced more headlines for affairs beyond the ropes, rather than what happens within, like Eddie Hearn and Dana White's feud, or whether Saul "Canelo" Alvarez and Christian Mbilli's bout should still proceed on Oct. 31 in Riyadh when the region is under threat from continued missile and drone strikes.
 Foster and Navarrete combined in Texas to remind critics what boxing can be like when it gets it right.
 Boxing can be brutal yet captivating, an art form, and one of the purest expressions of combat. Navarrete, a three-division champion, expresses that through wild shot-selection with hard punches thrown from unconventional angles. Foster, a two-time 130-pound champion, is meanwhile a technical master. Their clash of styles alone suggested Saturday's fight could become a classic — and boy, did it deliver.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The pace was unrelenting. The skill level was high. And the punches never stopped coming.
 If anybody was expecting a knockdown or knockout, Navarrete (40-3-1, 33 KOs) would likely have been the pick. However, the Mexican brawler struggled to find his rhythm throughout the early and middle rounds thanks to Foster's defensive acumen, and in the final round it was Foster (26-3, 12 KOs) who found two fight-sealing knockdowns, overpowering Navarrete during frenetic exchanges thanks to the timing of his right hands.
 It put the win beyond doubt for Foster, who secured a unanimous decision with scores of 118-108, 118-108 and 115-111.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I knew he was going to be strong, awkward," Foster said post-fight.
 "He's a great champion but I had a bit more in me tonight. I felt I was the better inside fighter and outside fighter, and I feel I proved it."
 Foster then aimed his sights directly at the winner of the Dec. 19 fight between WBA super featherweight champion Anthony Cacace and Nick Ball, calling for a chance to become the division's undisputed champion to kick off his 2027 campaign.
 Foster's victory wasn't the only notable win from the show, as Albert Gonzalez (19-0, 12 KOs) defeated Edward Vazquez (20-4, 6 KOs) with a second-round knockout in an exhilarating co-feature to thrust himself into possible title contention at featherweight.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Further down the card, Deric "Scooter" Davis (13-0, 10 KOs) out-finessed Joaquin Silva Faccio (10-2, 4 KOs) to win a unanimous decision after eight rounds, and, on the prelims, Sammy Contreras (9-0, 3 KOs) defeated Oscar Pedroza Padilla (8-3-1, 3 KOs) with a six-round win on points to announce himself as a considerable prospect.
 Main card results
 Unified super featherweight championship: O'Shaquie Foster (WBC) def. Emanuel Navarrete (WBO/IBF) via unanimous decision (115-111, 118-108, 118-108)
 Featherweight: Albert Gonzalez def. Edward Vazquez via second-round KO | Watch knockout 
 Super lightweight: Frank Martin def. Tarik Zaina via seventh-round TKO | Watch knockout 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Lightweight: Deric Davis def. Joaquin Silva Faccio via unanimous decision (80-72, 80-72, 80-72)
 Preliminary card results
 Lightweight: Sammy Contreras def. Oscar Pedroza Padilla via unanimous decision (60-54, 60-54, 60-54)
 Super bantamweight: Daniel Cortez III def. Joshua Montoya via split decision (58-56, 56-58, 58-56)
 Super welterweight: Joseph Almajdi def. Miqal Dolphus via unanimous decision (60-54, 60-54, 60-54)

 Foster said he'd be open to fighting Charly Suarez, the winner of Nick Ball and Anthony Cacace's fight, and would happily take on Shakur Stevenson, too.
